---
# Blog post template (decision 0015; style per AGENTS.md "Blog style").
# Copy to vignettes/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.qmd. The leading underscore keeps Quarto
# from rendering this template as a page.
#
# title: one declarative sentence, subject first, then the observed takeaway;
# never two fragments joined by a colon. Keep it in sync with
# VignetteIndexEntry below.
title: "SUBJECT does WHAT THE DATA SHOWED"
date: "YYYY-MM-DD"
# description states the FINDING (one declarative sentence), not the topic;
# shown in the blog index and used for meta description tags.
description: "DESCRIPTION, the finding in one sentence"
# followups feed later investigations and pipeline work; scan with grep across
# vignettes/ to find open threads.
followups:
  - "FOLLOWUP, an open question or next analysis"
# Default authorship unless the user says otherwise (project convention).
author:
  - "AI directed by Nick Giangreco"
# freeze: auto re-executes only when this post's source changes, so committed
# _freeze/ results keep data refreshes from re-running the chunk (dec 0015)
# while deliberate edits still propagate. Never use freeze: true: it serves
# the cached output even after the source is edited, so edits never deploy.
freeze: auto
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{SUBJECT does WHAT THE DATA SHOWED}
  %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# Load the package from the checkout with pkgload; no package install is
# required. Under altdoc the render runs in a temp dir, so resolve the root
# first (CFB2NFL_ROOT in the site build, else walk up to the _targets store).
root <- Sys.getenv("CFB2NFL_ROOT", "")
if (!nzchar(root)) {
  dir <- getwd()
  while (!file.exists(file.path(dir, "_targets")) && dirname(dir) != dir) {
    dir <- dirname(dir)
  }
  root <- if (file.exists(file.path(dir, "_targets"))) dir else getwd()
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
pkgload::load_all(root, quiet = TRUE)
con <- DBI::dbConnect(
  duckdb::duckdb(),
  file.path(root, "data", "cfb2nfl.duckdb"),
  read_only = TRUE
)
library(DBI)
library(dplyr)
library(duckdb)
library(ggiraph)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

# One interaction style for every girafe figure: a clear hover pop, dimming
# of non-hovered marks, a dark tooltip, and toolbar zoom + PNG download.
set_girafe_defaults(
  opts_hover = opts_hover(
    css = "stroke:#111827;stroke-width:2.5px;filter:brightness(1.12);"
  ),
  opts_hover_inv = opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.45;"),
  opts_tooltip = opts_tooltip(
    css = "background:#111827;color:#fff;padding:6px 9px;border-radius:5px;font-weight:bold;font-size:15px;"
  ),
  opts_zoom = opts_zoom(min = 1, max = 5),
  opts_toolbar = opts_toolbar(saveaspng = TRUE, position = "topright"),
  opts_sizing = opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE)
)

# thousands-separated and percent formatters for inline numbers
fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  formatC(as.numeric(x), big.mark = ",", format = "f", digits = digits)
}
pct <- function(x, digits = 1) sprintf("%.*f%%", digits, 100 * x)
```

```{r}
#| label: registry
#| include: false
# Key on athlete id, never name (recruiting ids collide, decision 0013).
# Declare every named subject's ids here so no exhibit hard-codes a name
# lookup.
subjects <- tibble::tribble(
  ~who          , ~cfb_athlete_id , ~gsis_id     ,
  "Example One" , "0000000"       , "00-0000000"
)
```

# queries, so a silent join change fails a unit test rather than a reader.
# Guard every pull so a broken query errors at authoring time, before the

## 1. Introduction

Then the expectations the Results sections test, one per line.

+ *Expectation one, as a claim the data can settle.*
+ *Expectation two.*

## 2. Data

### 2.1 ASSERTION ABOUT THE DATA (e.g. "Every eligible season ends in one of five statuses")

<!--
Sections follow one shape: an assertion heading, ONE OR TWO sentences saying
what the exhibits below show and why, then the exhibits. Every term a reader
meets later (unit of observation, statuses, groups) is defined here in a
table, in plain language, with reader-facing labels rather than column names.
-->

ONE OR TWO SENTENCES.

```{r}
#| label: terms
tibble::tribble(
  ~Term   , ~Meaning                  ,
  "TERM"  , "Plain-language meaning."
) |>
  kable(caption = "The terms used throughout.")
```

## 3. Results

### 3.1 ASSERTION THE SECTION DEMONSTRATES

*Expectation: the claim being tested.* ✅

<!--
ONE OR TWO sentences: what the exhibits show and why they are here. Any
further detail belongs in the table, a figure annotation, or a caption.
Exhibits follow in this order:
  1. table: expository, defines and counts what the claim rests on;
  2. explanatory figure: makes the claim at a glance, the claim's element
     highlighted (color, annotation, arrow), the rest context;
  3. exploratory figure: interactive view of the same snapshot at finer grain
     (every category, season, or player behind the claim), hover tooltips with
     the full detail.
A single-fact claim may drop to table plus one figure. Pin every number the
prose, captions, or annotations state.
-->

ONE OR TWO SENTENCES.
